correctness_confidence.basis: Positive target shares force positive payments in any exactly aligned solution. At doubling the positive-part denominator is at least two, so all subset constraints can safely be multiplied by it.

rigor.basis: The knots cover every possible sign change. For any box the certificate is a nonnegative combination of valid rows whose affine minimum on the simplex exceeds zero. Rounding is isolated from the acceptance checks.

novelty.basis: The level-set feasibility method and benefit-based cost allocation have precedents. The signed compensation model, exact share envelopes and comparison across information structures constitute a specific application.

significance.basis: The result quantifies how much geographic flexibility is lost by choosing shares early. The high-retention all-months scenario limits the value of information with this budget and worst-case objective.

reproducibility.basis: Both builds used immutable source inputs and yielded the same bytes. The archive contains the attributed source table, schedules, box multipliers and a standard-library verifier. It conditions on the published hydrological table.

summary: I participated in the analysis and writing and inspected the four pages of this canonical PDF. Rational upper schedules and box-wide lower certificates establish a narrow minimax interval for total variation across the eleven eligible scenarios. Most worst-case disagreement remains even with scenario-specific shares. The result concerns a modeled point-source project with a budget pegged to its incremental return.
strengths: Preserves the sign of credits and explicitly handles zero downstream benefit and negative return.
Distinguishes a single witness from coordinate ranges of near-optimal schedules.
Compares knowing calibration, knowing retention and knowing both using verifiable bounds.
weaknesses: Only eleven positive-return scenarios support the common proportional budget; interpolation or misspecification of the hydrology could affect all geographic ranges.
The relative rather than absolute budget can vary substantially in currency across scenarios.
A field deployment would require a separate assessment of fiscal capacity, fairness and alternative benefit measures.
potential_errors: The payer shares in the near-optimal intervals cannot be independently combined.
Interpreting total variation as a percentage change in measured water quality would misstate the estimand.
Using the separate policy experiment table with different project assumptions would not reproduce these bounds.
strong_novelty_candidates: Certified minimax and coordinatewise near-optimal contribution shares under uncertain hydrology and clipped initial net liabilities in this dataset.
